title: In the kitchen
summary: The imperative is the stem: Wacht even. Snijd de ui. One form for one person or more; zijn becomes wees. With u: stem + t + u (Komt u binnen). Ask with Kun je …? or Wil je …? Recipes and signs often use the infinitive.
explain:
The imperative (*de gebiedende wijs*) is the form for telling someone what to do: an order, an instruction, advice or an invitation. In the kitchen you hear it all the time: `Roer de saus`, `Pak een kom`, `Kom maar eten`. Dutch also has softer ways to ask, and recipes often use the infinitive instead.

### The form: the stem

The imperative is simply the **stem** of the verb, the same form as `ik` in the present tense (except for `zijn`, see below), with the same spelling rules (unit A2 · 01). There is no subject.

| infinitive | imperative |
| wachten | wacht |
| bakken | bak |
| lezen | lees |
| snijden | snijd |
| komen | kom |

> Wacht even, de pan is nog niet heet. — Wait a moment, the pan is not hot yet.
> Lees eerst het hele recept. — Read the whole recipe first.
> Snijd de ui in ringen. — Cut the onion into rings.

The form is the same for one person and for several: `Kom binnen!` to one friend, and `Kom binnen, jongens!` to a group.

Two verbs to learn by heart: `zijn` becomes `wees`, and `hebben` becomes `heb`.

> Wees voorzichtig met het mes. — Be careful with the knife.
> Heb even geduld. — Be patient for a moment.

### The formal form with u

To someone you say `u` to, use the u-form of the present tense and put `u` after it: stem + t + u. A stem that already ends in t gets no second t.

> Komt u binnen. — Come in. (formal)
> Gaat u zitten. — Sit down. (formal)
> Wacht u even. — Wait a moment. (formal)

### Word order

The imperative stands **first**. The rest of the sentence follows in the normal order:

- A **separable verb** splits: the prefix goes to the end. `Zet de oven aan`, `Bel me op`.
- A short pronoun comes straight after the verb: `Geef me het mes`.
- **niet** goes after the object, before the prefix or the place: `Zet de oven niet aan`, `Doe de pan niet in de vaatwasser`. With a noun that has `een` or no article you use **geen**: `Doe geen suiker in mijn thee`.

### Making it friendly: even, maar, eens

A bare imperative can sound bossy. Dutch speakers add a small word:

- `even`: only for a moment, it is no big deal. `Wacht even.`
- `maar`: go ahead, you may. `Kom maar binnen.`
- `eens`: just try, have a look. `Kijk eens.`

They stand after the verb and a short pronoun, before or after the object: `Geef me even het mes` and `Geef me het mes even` are both fine.

### Asking instead of ordering

Most polite of all is a question with a modal verb. The infinitive goes to the end.

> Kun je de oven aanzetten? — Can you switch on the oven?
> Wilt u even wachten? — Would you wait a moment, please? (formal)
> Mag ik het zout? — May I have the salt?

`Kan je` is just as correct; `Kun je` is a little more formal and more usual in writing. For "let's" Dutch says `Laten we` + infinitive: `Laten we beginnen` (more about `laten` in B1).

### The infinitive in recipes and on signs

Recipes, manuals and signs often give the infinitive instead of the imperative. Everything else comes first and the infinitive goes **last**, in one piece; often there is no article.

> De appels schillen en in stukken snijden. — Peel the apples and cut them into pieces.
> Niet roken. — No smoking.

### Watch out

- **No t.** *Snijdt de ui is wrong: the stem is `snijd`, written with d and pronounced as a t. `Snijd de ui.` (A form with -t for several people, as in `Komt allen`, is old-fashioned and survives only in old texts and songs.)
- **zijn is wees**: *Ben voorzichtig → `Wees voorzichtig`.
- **The prefix goes last**: *Opbel me → `Bel me op`.
- **niet does not come first**: *Niet raak de pan aan → `Raak de pan niet aan`. Only the infinitive takes `niet` in front: `Niet aanraken`.
- **With u the t comes back**: *Kom u binnen → `Komt u binnen`.

### Compared with Ukrainian

Ukrainian has two forms, `сідай` and `сідайте`. Dutch has one form for everyone you say `je` or `jullie` to, `Ga zitten`, and only `u` has its own form: `Gaat u zitten`.

words.en: to do the dishes / to wash up

sentences.note: The imperative of zijn is wees, a form of its own. Not ben, although ik ben is the ik-form.
aanzetten is separable: the imperative zet stands first and the prefix aan goes to the end.

sentences.nl: Pak maar een grote kom uit de kast.
sentences.en: Go ahead and take a big bowl from the cupboard.
sentences.note: pakken → stem pak, one k. Maar makes it an invitation: go ahead, you may.

sentences.nl: Doe de pan niet in de vaatwasser.
sentences.en: Don't put the pan in the dishwasher.
sentences.note: The imperative doe stands first. Niet comes after the object de pan and before the place in de vaatwasser.

sentences.nl: Voeg geen zout toe aan de soep.
sentences.en: Don't add any salt to the soup.
sentences.note: Zout has no article here, so the negative is geen, not niet. Toevoegen splits: voeg … toe.
alt: Voeg geen zout aan de soep toe.

sentences.nl: Gaat u zitten, het eten is bijna klaar.
sentences.en: Sit down (formal), the food is almost ready.
sentences.note: The formal imperative is the u-form of the verb with u after it: gaat u. Zitten is an infinitive and goes to the end.
alt: Gaat u maar zitten, het eten is bijna klaar.

sentences.nl: Kun je even de pannen afwassen?
sentences.en: Can you quickly wash the pans?
sentences.note: A question with kunnen is friendlier than an order. Kun je: jij loses its t after the verb, and the infinitive afwassen stays in one piece at the end.
alt: Kun je de pannen even afwassen?
Kun jij even de pannen afwassen?
Kun jij de pannen even afwassen?
Kan je even de pannen afwassen?
Kan je de pannen even afwassen?
Kan jij even de pannen afwassen?
Kan jij de pannen even afwassen?

sentences.nl: Bel me even op als het eten klaar is.
sentences.en: Just give me a call when the food is ready.
sentences.note: opbellen splits in the imperative: bel … op. The pronoun me comes straight after bel, and even after the pronoun.
alt: Bel mij even op als het eten klaar is.
Bel me even als het eten klaar is.
Bel mij even als het eten klaar is.

sentences.nl: Twee theelepels suiker toevoegen en goed roeren.
sentences.en: Add two teaspoons of sugar and stir well. (recipe style, with the infinitive)
sentences.note: A recipe can use the infinitive instead of the imperative. The infinitive goes last, and toevoegen stays in one piece.

sentences.nl: Laten we eerst de appels schillen.
sentences.note: Laten we + infinitive is Dutch for 'let's'. Laten stands first, we follows, and schillen goes to the end.
alt: Laten we de appels eerst schillen.

exercises.nl: ___ de ui op de snijplank, niet op tafel.
exercises.en: Cut the onion on the chopping board, not on the table.
exercises.note: The imperative is the stem: snijden → snijd. It sounds like a t, but it is written with d, as in ik snijd.

exercises.en: Be careful, the pan is hot!
exercises.note: zijn has its own imperative: wees. Ben and bent are present-tense forms and cannot give an order.

exercises.nl: Doe ___ suiker in mijn thee, alsjeblieft.
exercises.en: Don't put any sugar in my tea, please.
exercises.note: Suiker stands without de or het, so the negative is geen. Niet is for a verb or for a noun with de, het or a possessive.

exercises.nl: ___ u binnen, de koffie is klaar.
exercises.en: Come in (formal), the coffee is ready.
exercises.note: With u the imperative is the u-form of the present tense: u komt, so Komt u. The bare stem kom is for je and jullie.

exercises.nl: ___ (hebben) even geduld, de taart is bijna gaar.
exercises.en: Be patient for a moment, the cake is almost done.
exercises.note: The imperative of hebben is heb, the same as the ik-form. Not hebt or heeft.

exercises.nl: ___ (bakken) de uien vijf minuten in een beetje boter.
exercises.en: Fry the onions for five minutes in a little butter.
exercises.note: The imperative is the stem, and a stem never ends in a double consonant: bakken → bak.
lezen → stem lees: the long e is written double, and z becomes s at the end of a word.

answers: Zet de oven nog niet aan.
exercises.en: Don't switch the oven on yet.
exercises.note: The imperative stands first and the prefix aan goes to the end. Nog niet comes after the object, before the prefix.

answers: Kun je even de kom pakken?
Kun je de kom even pakken?
exercises.en: Can you just get the bowl?
exercises.note: A polite question: Kun je first, the infinitive pakken last. Even may stand before or after de kom.

answers: De appels schillen en in stukken snijden.
exercises.en: Peel the apples and cut them into pieces. (recipe style)
exercises.note: In a recipe the infinitive comes last in each part: de appels schillen, then in stukken snijden.

answers: Laten we samen de pannen afwassen.
Laten we de pannen samen afwassen.
exercises.note: Laten we + infinitive for 'let's'. The infinitive afwassen goes last; samen may stand before or after de pannen.

exercises.from: Wacht even, de soep is nog niet klaar.
answers: Wacht u even, de soep is nog niet klaar.
exercises.en: Wait a moment (formal), the soup is not ready yet.
exercises.note: The formal form is stem + t + u. The stem wacht already ends in t, so it stays wacht: Wacht u even.

exercises.task: Turn the order into a polite question with Kunt u.
answers: Kunt u me het recept sturen?
Kunt u mij het recept sturen?
exercises.en: Could you send me the recipe? (formal)
exercises.note: Kunt u stands first, and sturen moves to the end as an infinitive. Me stays right after the subject u.

exercises.task: Write it as a recipe would: with the infinitive instead of the imperative.
exercises.from: Bak de uien in de pan.
answers: De uien in de pan bakken.
De uien bakken in de pan.
exercises.en: Fry the onions in the pan.
exercises.note: With the infinitive, the object comes first and the verb goes to the end: de uien in de pan bakken.

exercises.wrong: Opbel me als het eten klaar is.
answers: Bel me op als het eten klaar is.
Bel mij op als het eten klaar is.
Bel me als het eten klaar is.
exercises.en: Call me when the food is ready.
exercises.note: opbellen is separable. In the imperative it splits: bel stands first, op goes to the end of the main clause.

exercises.wrong: Niet raak de pan aan, hij is heet.
answers: Raak de pan niet aan, hij is heet.
exercises.en: Don't touch the pan, it is hot.
exercises.note: The imperative always stands first; niet comes later, before the prefix aan. Niet at the start only goes with an infinitive: Niet aanraken.
